MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AT KUNDAPURA, ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 27.09.2018 passed in MVC No.891/2016 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and Addl.
Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal at Kundapura, (for short 'the Tribunal'),

sentences.text: the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01.04.2016 at about 8.45 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-20- EK-5846 from Hengavalli side towards Ulumundu side and when he reached near Narayana Kulal house at Ulumundu Hengevalli village, Kundapura Taluk, another motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-20-EK-4747 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.2-insurance company came and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.

Because of which, petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Deformity of foot with loss of 3-4th toe at MTP Joint, Loss of 2-5th toes at TPX.
2. Various deformity great toe.
3. Uneven scar over foot.
4. Stance phase reduced.
5. Forefoot - Middfoot movements reduced by 30%.
6. Dorsiflexion - Planter flexion reduced by 30%.
7. X-ray shows Ostroporosis.

Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2016.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.

Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.9,500/-
per month.
The petitioner was aged 40 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the multiplier of 15 has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

sentences.text: Towards 'pain and suffering', a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, in my opinion it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.
Towards 'hospital and medical expenses', a sum of Rs.54,157/- is awarded.
As the same is based on the actual bills submitted, I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'loss of amenities', a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.

Towards 'food, nourishment, attendant charges and transportation charges', taking into consideration the injuries as well as the hospital expenses, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads are modified as hereunder:-
Sl.
 Head Rs. Ps.
 No.
 Future loss of future earning  1 Rs.2,56,500-00  capacity  2 Pain sufferings Rs.40,000-00  3 Hospital and medical expenses Rs.54,157-00  Loss of income during laid up  4 Rs.28,500-00  period  5 Loss of amenities Rs.40,000-00  Food, nourishment, attendant  6 charges and transportation Rs.20,000-00  charges

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.88,600/- (Rs.4,39,157/- minus Rs.3,50,557/-). Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
